Anwar Hossain (Md)  ------- Appellant

full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah J: This Criminal Appeal at the instance of Md Anwar Hossain under section 24 of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain, 1995 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Ain') is directed against the judgment and order dated 19-7- 2001 passed by the learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Daman)Tribunal (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal') Shariatpur in Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Case No.1 of 2000 convicting accused appellant Md Anwar Hossain under section 9(Ga) of the Ain, sentencing him thereunder to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 10(ten) years and also to pay a fine of Taka 20,000 in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for a period of 2(two) years more. 

 2. Prosecution case, stated briefly, is that on 13-10-1999, one Raihana Khatun lodged a first information report with Palong Police Station to the effect that on the aforesaid date, the informant met her distant relation (maternal cousin) Raihan Mollah at Zagira bus stand while he proposed to take her to Shariatpur to enjoy cinema show; that informant readily accepted his proposal and accordingly, she went to Shariatpur and enjoyed a film 'Kazar Maya' by name in the "Alochaya Cinema Hall" and that they also moved to different places and in the evening, Raihan told the informant that there is no bus or other means of communication to go to Zagira, so they are to stay in a hotel for the night. It is further stated that the informant could understand the fraudulent intention of accused Raihan. The informant insisted to go to Zagira at any cost and that at about 6-00 PM in the evening Raihan took the informant to AI-Russell Hotel and took a room on rent. It is further stated that at about 7-45 PM, when Raihan went to bathroom, 4 persons came to their room and an elderly person knocked at the door for which the informant opened the door and these persons told her that they are members of police force and have come from the police station as they were there illegally and wanted to take her to police station. The informant wanted in all earnestness to get rid of Raihan for which she set sail for the police station with them but they took her in a kachcha house and wanted to rape her and as she raised hue and cry, those persons got frightened and set her free and thereafter took her to the house of one Abdul Mannan who could easily understand their motive and took her to the Chairman of Pourashava wherefrom the informant was taken to Palong Police Station where she lodged the first information report. Hence the present case. 

 4. The case ultimately, came to the Court of the learned Judge, Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan ) Adalat, Shariatpur which was registered as Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan case No. 01 of 2000 and the learned Judge, on the basis of the materials available on record, framed charge against the accused Md Anwar Hossain under section 9(Ga) of the Ain and read it over to him in open Court to which he pleaded not guilty and demanded trial. 

 6. The defence case as it transpires from the trend of cross examination of the PWs and the suggestions put forward on his behalf is that he is innocent and he has been falsely implicated in the case out of previous enmity and grudge. 

 7. On. consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record, the learned Judge was pleased to award the conviction against accused Md Anwar Hossain under section 9 (Ga) of the Ain and sentenced him thereunder to suffer imprisonment for 10(ten) years and also to pay a fine of Taka 20,000 in default to suffer rigorous imprisonment for 2(two) years more. 

 8. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the conviction and sentence dated 19-7-2001 passed by the learned Judge of the Adalat, Shariatpur in Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Case No.1 of 2000, the appellant has come up with the present appeal which is opposed by the respondent State through the learned Assistant Attorney-General. 

 9. Mr Kazi Shahadat Hossain, the learned Advocate for the present appellant, took us through the FIR, charge sheet, charge so framed, the deposition of the prosecution witnesses, the impugned judgment and order and the materials available in the paper book and submits that appellant is quite innocent and he has been falsely implicated in this case out of previous enmity and grudge; that the trial Court did not apply his judicial mind in analysing the deposition of PWs and their cross-examinations and that the learned trial Court has based his judgment on surmises and conjectures and not on legal evidence on record. He further submits that the prosecution has miserably failed to prove the case against the appellant Md Anwar Hossain and that the order of conviction and sentence is bad in law as well as on facts and circumstances of the case and, as such, the impugned judgment and order of conviction and sentence is liable to be set aside. 

 10. Mr SM Shahjahan Kabir, the learned Assistant Attorney-General for the State, on the other hand, submits that the prosecution has proved its case against the appellant by most consistent, corroborative, overwhelming and competent witnesses. He further submits that the learned Judge of the Adalat was perfectly justified in convicting and sentencing the appellant on the basis of the most cogent and reliable evidence and that his judgment does not suffer from any misreading and non-reading of evidence. He further submits that all the prosecution witnesses are natural, probable and competent witnesses and there is no internal points of falsehood in their evidence on any point and, as such, the impugned judgment calls for no interference by this Court. 

 12. PW 1, Raihana Khatun, is the informant of that the victim was taken by police from hotel to this case who deposed that the accused Raihan Mollah is her cousin who took her to Shariatpur on her own request; that the accused Raihan Mollah firstly did not agree to take her to Shariatpur and thereafter he accepted her proposal to take her there for the purpose of watching cinema. She further adds that due to 'golmal' there, bus connection was suspended and, as such, they hired a room in a hotel named Al- Russell at Shariatpur and thereafter 3/4 persons went there who said they were police personnel and wanted to take her to the police station and she agreed to their proposal in order to get rid of the hand of Raihan Mollah and they took her to an unknown place nearby and they made attempt to commit rape on her but because of her resistance they left her in another homestead nearby and subsequently she came to know that it was homestead of the local Chairman on whose information police also came and recovered her. Thereafter she was taken to Thana and as per her statement, FIR was drafted and the contents of which were read out to her and being found correct, she signed the ejahar which is marked as Exhibit 1 and her signature therein is marked as Exhibit 1/1. 

 22. PW 5, Bhuiyan Mahbub Hasan, is the investigating officer of this case. He investigated the case and submitted charge sheet against all the accused persons. He also proves FIR Form Exhibit 1 (A) and signature Exhibit 1A/1 therein. He also proves the sketch maps Exhibits 3 and 4 with separate index Exhibits 3A, 4A and. his signatures respectively Exhibits 3/1, 4/1, 3A/1 and 4A/1 therein. He denied the defence suggestion that the accused persons are innocent or that he found no evidence against them. 

 2.	Whether the verdict of conviction and sentence awarded upon convict appellant can be sustained in law, evidence, materials on record, the facts and circumstances of the case and also in the true dispensation of justice; and 

 25. In approaching and answering to the points drawn up, the cardinal principles of criminal jurisprudence in awarding conviction followed by sentence upon an indicted person demands meditation. A legal survey of law, appraisal of evidence, browsing eye on materials brought on record, analysis of fact and circumstance of the case, inherent infirmities disturbing and striking facts of prosecution case are also required to be taken into consideration. Rival contentions surged forward from both sides shall be also addressed and considered by us. 

 26. Fundamental principles of criminal jurisprudence and justice delivery system is the innocence of the alleged accused and he should be presumed to be innocent until the charges are proved beyond reasonable doubt on the basis of clear, cogent and credible evidence and that onus of proving everything essential to the establishment of charge against accused lies upon the prosecution which must prove charge substantially as laid to the hilt and beyond all reasonable doubt on the strength of clear, cogent, credible and unimpeachable evidence. In a criminal trial, the burden of proving the guilt of the accused beyond all reasonable doubts always rest on the prosecution and on its failure, it cannot fall back upon the evidence adduced by the accused in support of his defence to rest its case solely thereon. Proof of charge must depend upon judicial evaluation of totality of evidence, oral and circumstantial and not by an isolated scrutiny. Prosecution version is also required to be judged taking into account overall circumstances of the case with a practical, pragmatic and reasonable approach in appreciation of evidence let in to drive home guilt of accused person. 

 27. It is always to be remembered that justice delivery system cannot be carried away by heinous nature of crime or by gruesome manner in which it was found to have been committed and graver the charge is greater is the standard of proof required. It should also be borne in mind that if the accused can create any doubts by adducing evidence or cross- examining the PWs in the prosecution case the accused is entitled to get benefit of doubt. It is conveniently observed that though sad, yet it is a fact that in our country, there is a tendency on the part of the people to rope in as many people as possible for facing trial in respect of any criminal case. It has been even found that innocent persons including aged, infirm, rivals are booked for standing on dock. Some are acquitted by the Court of first instance and some by appellate Court, but only after having been in incarceration for years. Such efforts on the part of relatives of victim and other interested persons invariably are done and thus it becomes difficult on the part of a Court to find out the real culprit. Under such circumstances and in view of the prevalent criminal jurisprudential system, a judge is to find out the truth from a bundle of lies and to shift the grain out of chaff. A Judge does not preside over a criminal trial merely to see that no innocent person is punished. A judge also presides to see that guilty man does not escape. Both are public duties. Law therefore, cannot afford any favour other than the truth and only truth. 

 29. Now let us see whether the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence on record fall under the purview of section 9(Ga) of the Ain. Aforesaid provision of section 9(Ga) are as follows: 

 30. In the definition of section 2 of the said Ain, the words প্রলুদ্ধ করিয়া বা ফুসলাইয়া have not been defined. Section 361 of the Penal Code has defined the offence of kidnapping of a minor or a person of unsound mind from lawful guardianship and has used the word "Entices" in that section. Meaning of the word "entice" in Bengali according to the Samsad English dictionary is প্রভাবিত করা বা বিপথে চালিত করা and according to the Bangla Academy English to Bengali Dictionary প্ররোচিত করা অথবা প্রলোভন দেখান and meaning of the word enticement according to the said Dictionary is প্ররোচনা প্রলোভন Meaning of the word ফুসলানো and according to AT Dev's Student Favourite Dictionary (Bengali to English) is Cajole, Coax, Flatter, Seduce, Entice, lure away. On the other hand, meaning of the word প্রলুদ্ধ in English, according to the said dictionary is "allured, tempted". Thus it appears that the words প্রলুদ্ধ করিয়া বা ফুসলাইয়া  have been used in the said section 9(Ga) to mean, "to entice away any person". Section 367 of the Penal Code has defined the offence of abduction to mean taking away by compelling a person by force or by inducing such a person by deceitful means. Thus we find that in the case of kidnapping a minor or a person of unsound mind from the custody of a lawful guardian, there is no question of compelling the minor under sixteen years of age by force but in a case of abducting a person being a minor or major, there is the question of compelling the person by force or inducing by deceitful means. 

 31. Section 3 of the said Ain provides that provision of the Ain shall remain in force notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force. So, the provisions of section 9 of the Ain shall remain in force and the provisions of the Penal Code regarding kidnapping and abducting to the extent which is in conflict with the provision of section 9 of the Ain shall have no force. Since the definition of kidnapping or abduction have neither been given in section 2 of the Ain nor definition of those offences has been adopted from the Penal Code, the word 'অপহরণ" used in section 9 is to be understood in the context in which it has been used in the said section. In the clause (Ga) the word 'অপহরণ" has been used in the context of বল প্রয়োগ করিয়া বা ফুসলাইয়া যৌন সংগম করিতে বাধ্য করার উদ্দেশ্যে We have already seen the meaning of the word প্রলুদ্ধ is "allured or tempted" and ফুসলানো is "cajole", coax, flatter, seduce, entice, lure away". In the instant case though there is no evidence of forcibly taking away the victim which means in Bengali বল প্রয়োগে ঘটনার শিকারকে নিয়ে যাওয়া but there is no evidence of প্রলুদ্ধ করিয়া  (by cajoling or coaxing or flattering or seducing, or enticing or luring away) the victim girl for the purpose of compelling her to submit to sexual intercourse যৌন সংগম করিতে বাধ্য করার উদ্দেশ্যে.  In section 9 of the Ain, the words কোন নারীকে any woman have been used without mentioning minor or major. So, the words কোন নারীকে means any girl or woman irrespective of her age. Taking away of a girl or a woman irrespective of her age by using force or by giving her allurement or temptation or by coaxing or cajoling or flattering or seducing or enticing her for the purpose of compelling her to submit to sexual intercourse with another person will attract the offence under clause (Ga) of section 9 of the said Ain. 

 32. In the instant case we have already seen that the victim girl Raihana was not taken away by using force or by giving her allurement or temptation or by coaxing or cajoling or flattering or seducing or enticing her for the purpose of compelling her to submit to sexual intercourse. 

 34. In this case we have already noticed the charge framed by the Court below which is not in conformity with prosecution case. In this respect we like to point out that in a criminal case, framing of charge properly is very important. It is the function of the conducting lawyer like the Public Prosecutor to assist the Court to frame charge properly on the basis of the materials on the record of the case and documents submitted therewith and it is the duty of the judge to frame charge after perusing the record and documents therewith and hearing the parties and examining, if any, the accused. In the case of Nazrul Islam vs State reported in 50 DLR 103 it has been pointed out that in framing charge, Court is to follow the provisions of sections 221, 223 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and, as such, we do not like to reiterate the same here. If the charge is not properly framed in conformity with the prosecution case and evidence led in support of the same, the charge is liable to fall through, benefit of which goes in favour of the accused. Though an accused is charged with one offence he may be convicted for another kind of offence if the allegations made in the charge are proved beyond reasonable doubt. On the other hand, the accused cannot be convicted if the allegations made in the charge constituting the offence are not substantiated by unimpeachable evidence. In the instant case, the charge against the accused appellant was not framed properly nor was the charge proved beyond reasonable doubt by unimpeachable evidence. 

 35. The main point for determination in this case is, whether the accused appellant abducted the victim and whether any witness has recognised the accused appellant Md Anwar Hossain to take away the victim Raihana from the Hotel Al-Russell. 

 36. It is a settled principle that in a case of sexual offence, the prosecutrix is the best witness to prove whether the accused committed any offence. Legally speaking, corroboration of the prosecution evidence is not a must for awarding a conviction, but as a matter of practice, it has become a judicial prudence that the evidence of the prosecution witnesses should, whenever practicable, be corroborated in material particulars. 

 47. Now we turn to the defence case that the accused appellant Md Anwar Hossain is quite innocent. He is in no way connected with the alleged occurrence and he has been falsely implicated in this case. It further appears from the submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant that the appellant Md Anwar Hossain is a police personnel aged about 55 years. He has a professional enmity with the investigating officer who has entangled him in this case out of grudge. We find substance in the submission of the learned Advocate for the appellant because he filed a perfunctory charge sheet without any basis. 

 Secondly, for the purpose of intercourse. Unless a woman is taken away forcibly by a person for the purpose of intercourse, the scope of section 9(Ga) will not attract. In the instant case, neither of these two ingredients has been proved. In fact, it is a case of no evidence. 

 50. We receive support of the above view in the case of Shafiqul Islam (Md) vs State reported in 50 DLR 581. 

 54. The learned Court below, has failed to apply its judicial mind to the evidence on record, rather convicted accused appellant purely on surmises and conjectures as a result of which serious miscarriage of justice has taken place in this case calling for interference by this Court. 

 55. Scanning the evidence of this case in the light of the above mentioned standard of proof, we are of the view that the prosecution has totally failed to prove the case beyond all reasonable doubt. 

 56. Considering these facts and circumstances of this case and evidence or record, we are of the view that there is no evidence in the four comers of the record that the accused appellant abducted the victim for the purpose of intercourse and thus we find that the prosecution has, in fact, adduced no evidence to connect the accused appellant in the offence of abduction for immoral purpose punishable under section 9(Ga) of the Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan (Bishesh Bidhan) Ain 1995. 

 57. The trial Court failed to assess the evidence of witnesses in its true perspective. The trial Court erred both in law and on facts in not considering the highly improbable story of the prosecution case and failed to consider the inherent defects in the prosecution story because the informant has given different versions about the so-called incident at different times. 

 58. The learned trial Court failed to examine the accused appellant properly while examining him under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure as a result of which the accused appellant could not take proper defence in this case occasioning failure of justice. 

 59. In the light of the above findings, we are satisfied that the prosecution has failed to establish the case against the accused appellant beyond all reasonable doubt and, as such, the appellant is liable to be acquitted of the charge levelled against him punishable under section 9(Ga) of the Ain.
